content.user_title: Design Apple Platform Interfaces with HIG Guidance
content.value_statement: Apple apps often lose quality when one design is copied across every platform. This skill provides platform-specific HIG guidance for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, and games.
actual_capabilities: Compares platform interaction models across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, and games.
Recommends navigation, input, layout, and presentation patterns for each Apple platform.
Guides adaptation of one app concept across phone, tablet, desktop, TV, spatial, and watch contexts.
Summarizes platform characteristics such as display, ergonomics, inputs, and system features.
Includes game-specific guidance for controllers, menus, immersion, accessibility, and platform services.
Prompts for missing product context before giving platform-specific recommendations.
limitations: It is a static guidance skill and may not include later Apple HIG updates.
It does not replace testing on real Apple devices and simulators.
It does not generate visual assets, prototypes, or implementation code by itself.
It focuses on platform design decisions, not App Store policy review.

use_cases.title: Adapt an iPhone App for iPad and Mac
use_cases.description: Map mobile navigation and touch patterns to larger screens, sidebars, windows, keyboard input, and pointer interactions.

use_cases.title: Plan Platform-Specific Engineering Notes
use_cases.description: Create implementation notes for input methods, layout behavior, safe areas, multitasking, and platform conventions.

use_cases.title: Align Game UX Across Apple Devices
use_cases.description: Review controller support, in-game menus, accessibility, display sizes, and immersive behavior for Apple game releases.

prompt_templates.title: Get Platform Basics
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner overview for a single target platform.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the key HIG design differences for a new app on iOS. Include input, navigation, layout, and system feature expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt One Screen
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn an existing mobile screen into a platform-aware layout.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have an iPhone screen with tabs, a list, and a detail view. Recommend how it should adapt for iPadOS and macOS.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Platform Options
prompt_templates.scenario: Choose which Apple platforms deserve distinct designs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, and visionOS for a personal finance app. Focus on use context and interaction model.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multi-Platform Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced guidance for a coordinated product system.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a platform adaptation plan for a multi-platform Apple app. Include recommendations, differences table, implementation notes, and questions for unresolved context.

output_examples.input: A team wants to move an iPhone task manager to iPadOS and macOS.
output_examples.output: The response compares tab bars, sidebars, window resizing, keyboard shortcuts, and multitasking. It recommends adapting workflows instead of copying the phone layout.

output_examples.input: A studio asks how a game menu should work on Apple platforms.
output_examples.output: The response covers readable text, flexible aspect ratios, controller support, touch controls, accessibility options, and full-screen or immersive contexts.

output_examples.input: A founder asks whether a wellness app should support watchOS and visionOS.
output_examples.output: The response contrasts glanceable watch interactions with spatial visionOS experiences. It identifies suitable features and areas that need product validation.

best_practices: Start with the user context and target platforms before requesting detailed design recommendations.
Ask for separate guidance when one feature behaves differently across phone, tablet, desktop, TV, spatial, and watch contexts.
Verify final decisions against current Apple documentation and device testing before release.
anti_patterns: Do not copy a single iPhone layout directly to every Apple platform.
Do not ignore input differences such as touch, pointer, remote, Digital Crown, gaze, and gesture.
Do not treat this skill as a substitute for accessibility review or usability testing.

faq.question: Which Apple platforms does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, and Apple game design guidance.

faq.question: Can it help port an app from iPhone to iPad or Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare navigation, layout, input, and system conventions so the design adapts to each platform.

faq.question: Does it provide implementation code?
faq.answer: No. It provides design recommendations and implementation notes, but it does not generate production code by itself.

faq.question: Does it replace Apple documentation?
faq.answer: No. It summarizes and applies platform guidance, but teams should verify decisions against current Apple documentation.

faq.question: Can it help with game design?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Apple platform guidance for game controls, menus, display adaptation, accessibility, and immersive experiences.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
